ownership_reason: Only the gold decides the node for a define value: hop 1 creates and returns the result map, hops 2 and 3 hand the values and the map on, and hop 4 hands each value to the gold and puts the returned node under the define's name, without looking at the value. The gold's javadoc promises a new node whose value is the given value; the variant gold gives the boolean true a string node whose value is the text "true", so testDefineFlag's boolean defines come out as "true". The variant gold creates only number and string nodes, so no caller can pre-filter a value into a TRUE node; restoring them needs a caller that tests the values itself and creates the TRUE/FALSE nodes instead of the gold. The convention is pinned outside the gold: CompilerOptions.setDefineToBooleanLiteral sets a define 'to a boolean literal', DefaultPassConfig.getAdditionalReplacements replaces the COMPILED define by new Node(Token.TRUE), NodeUtil.isValidDefineValue accepts TRUE and FALSE as define values, and AbstractCommandLineRunner.createDefineReplacements turns the texts true and false into boolean defines; ProcessDefinesTest::testOverriding1 (boolean defines replaced by TRUE/FALSE nodes) passes, as do CompilerOptionsTest::testDefines and CommandLineRunnerTest::testDefineFlag2 / testDefineFlag3 (number and string nodes through the chain).
